findings.title: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu while BuildIndex writes it concurrently
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock. `BuildIndex` writes the map at lines 137-139 under `cacheMu`, but a reader that takes no lock is not excluded. Two callers read the map this way. `BleveIndexMetrics.Collect` calls it on every Prometheus scrape (`pkg/storage/unified/resource/bleve_index_metrics.go:96`). This PR adds a second call at `resource/search.go:216`. This PR also removes the lock that covered the whole of `BuildIndex`. Index builds from `getOrCreateIndex` (search requests and watch events) and from the init workers can therefore run while a scrape iterates the map. Concurrent map read and write is a data race. The Go runtime can detect it and abort the process with `fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write`. Fix: take `b.cacheMu.RLock()` in `TotalDocs`. Better still, snapshot the indexes under the lock and call `DocCount` outside it.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same key; the replaced index is never closed
findings.body: The old code held `cacheMu` for the whole of `BuildIndex`. That serialized builds and also blocked `GetIndex`, which was the latency problem. The lock is now taken only for the map write. `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` (`resource/search.go:287-307`) has no per-key de-duplication, so two requests that both see a missing index will both build it. For memory indexes the second `b.cache[key] = idx` silently replaces the first. Events written through an index the caller still holds are then lost, and the replaced bleve index is never closed. `IndexTenants` is also incremented twice. For file indexes the second `bleve.New(dir)` fails because the directory already exists. That failure was already possible, since the old code also built twice sequentially. Consider re-checking the cache under the write lock before storing, closing the loser, or using singleflight per key.

findings.title: Stop() no longer rejects requests, because request handlers stopped calling Init and nothing else reads initErr
findings.body: Every handler used to call `s.Init(ctx)`, which returns `s.initErr`. `Stop` sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" or "service is stopped" (lines 321-339). After shutdown starts, requests were therefore rejected with that error. This PR removes all of those calls. The only remaining reader of `initErr` is `Init` itself, which runs once in the constructor. Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search and the blob calls now proceed against a stopped backend and a cancelled context, and fail with unrelated errors or hang. If the guard is meant to go, `Stop` should not keep setting `initErr`, and the fields and comments around it are now misleading. If it is meant to stay, handlers should check a stopped flag (an atomic bool or `initErr` under a lock). Reading `initErr` from the handlers without synchronization would race with `Stop`.

findings.title: Postgres skip is unrelated to the PR and hides a possible regression
findings.body: This test is skipped for postgres with the reason "Works locally" and a TODO. Resource server init now happens at construction (`resource/server.go:258`). Failing in CI only is exactly what a startup-ordering or timing change would cause. Please check that this PR did not introduce the failure, and link a tracking issue in the TODO. If it is unrelated, move the skip to a separate PR.

contracts.action: Server initialization (lifecycle, search index, watcher) moved from lazy per-request s.Init to NewResourceServer
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously each handler (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob) called s.Init(ctx), a sync.Once that returned the cached initErr, including the error Stop() stored.
contracts.before_after: Before: first request ran init with the request ctx, and every later request returned initErr, including 'service is stopping/stopped' after Stop. After: init runs once in the constructor with the server's internal admin-claims ctx, and failure aborts construction. Handlers never re-check state, so Stop's initErr is unreachable by requests. Order is also changed to search.init before initWatcher.
contracts.visible_effect: Startup is slower and synchronous. Init errors now fail startup instead of the first API call. Requests after Stop are no longer rejected up front.
contracts.failure_mode: If lifecycle.Init or search.init fails, NewResourceServer returns an error and the caller fails. After Stop, handlers run against a cancelled context and a stopped backend.

contracts.action: bleveBackend.BuildIndex takes cacheMu only around the cache write, and searchSupport.init now logs TotalDocs
contracts.equivalent_path: GetIndex takes cacheMu.RLock for reads. TotalDocs (also called from bleve_index_metrics.go:96) reads the map with no lock.
contracts.before_after: Before: BuildIndex held the write lock for the entire build, which serialized builds and blocked GetIndex. After: the lock is held only for the map assignment. TotalDocs is still unlocked and is now also called in init.
contracts.visible_effect: Search requests are no longer blocked by index builds. Concurrent same-key builds can duplicate work or replace an index.
contracts.failure_mode: A concurrent map read in TotalDocs, from a scrape or the init log, against a write in BuildIndex can crash the process with a fatal concurrent map error.

summary: The change moves resource server init into the constructor and narrows the bleve cache lock. It has two real problems: `TotalDocs` reads the cache map with no lock while builds now write it concurrently, and `Stop()` no longer causes requests to be rejected because the handlers stopped reading `initErr`. Smaller notes cover duplicate concurrent builds, the heavier constructor, and the unrelated postgres test skip. The tracer ctx reassignments, the logger swaps and the log removal look fine.
